reviews.review: Most addictive startup ever.

I know we all hate super hand-holdy games but this goes so far in the opposite direction it's not even fun. There are many unintuitive mechanics/design choices that your only real option to understand how to play is to watch some videos on how to play. Incredibly lazy decisions made by the developer, I would not buy this game at regular price or even half price. It's also quite a hostile experience trying to play with a controller, so don't even bother. I'm sure it'll get better but everything feels so stiff and clunky - this is not a game that feels good to play, maybe it feels good to overcome... I'm getting a refund though and maybe I'll give it another go if it dips below $5.

I'm glad I caught myself before the 2 hour refund limit because some of the other reviews speak to issues that I wouldn't discover unless going much deeper into the game. If the controls weren't stiff and clunky, and they took 10 minutes to explain the basic mechanics of managing your raft (my first game I went to check out an island, my raft floated away, resources in the water despawned when my raft left, and I didn't have enough resources to build a new one, didn't know things could only be built on the raft, etc ,etc.)

It's also far to easy too die and far too punishing when you do, so the game itself doesn't even encourage learning how to play by playing. Maybe it's more fun if you have 4 people to gather resources, stab boars, and manage a single raft - but for me this was just 2 hours of my life wasted and filled with frustration.

I like the concept of this survival game. Building your raft into a mobile base/ floating factory that you take with you thoughout your journey, upgrading it along the way from story location to the next one.

Despite the graphics not being the greatest, it does not stop me from enjoying exploring above and under water.

The game lacks a bit in tutorials. In the beginning it is difficult to know what you exactly need to do, requiring watching Youtube and reading the wiki to get started. But once I picked up the basics, the game become much more enjoyable to play. 
Another thing that is a bit annoying is the low durability of most equipment, requiring you to replace it along the way quite frequently or to have a spare one ready whenever you are exploring a large island.

A lovely survival/build game with an element of adventure, and a breezy aesthetic. The building mechanics are straight-forward, but definitely branch out into some items which require and absurdly stingy amount of resources. Still, it was very fun to customize the raft, and get it feeling like a floating home. Great for co-ops, since I can’t imagine playing this alone. The story mode was good, but did feel like it wore out its welcome by the end. Definitely great fodder for a game night, and well worth the price it's sold at.

I really enjoyed this game. It was awesome sailing around and exploring the islands and building a raft. I played co-op with a friend and it was cool watching our raft expand overtime to something gigantic. It's also a game you can just chill and relax with. There wasn't a rush to get things done and we could do them at our own pace. We 100% this game getting all 104/104 achievements which took us 80 something hours to get. I found it extremely hard and very grindy to get some of the end game achievements but worth it once it added another perfect game to my list. I highly recommend this game playing by yourself or with your friends. You won't regret it.

Definitely made for playing with friends and it's the most fun when you don't take anything seriously. The main campaign took about 25-30 hours for me which is a really solid length. I didn't pay attention to any of the story whatsoever but it didn't really detract from the whole experience at all. The gameplay is fun and the progression is pretty rewarding. Building the raft was a lot more fun than I expected and it's nice when each one of your friends has a different role to fulfill - i can imagine it would get stressful doing everything by yourself.
TLDR: Really fun game but don't play it if you don't have friends.

While not the most glamorous of games, this is still a recommendation from me, as the survival system is engrossing enough to keep exploring just about until the end of the story.

It's relatively easy to just stick to the story to get through it as quick as one would like. But I'd posit anyone trying Raft out, to try and explore the game as more of a checklist - I know, sounds riveting. But the ideas are nice, and it's never all that difficult to posit a frustrated response either. And definitely play it with friends. It's not quite the full jank of atmospheres, but the comedic atmosphere and general whimsical nature of the game is to be enjoyed when exacerbated by someone laughing in your ear.

It's a nice ride. And a polished one at that. Don't expect to remember much of the story details after, but if you're fishing for a few nice evenings with friends, I very much recommend giving this a shot.
